label: copy-phase input i (fed-back original token 2-4), not on the last step
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is the letter i (99.8% of mass has in_tok == i). This happens when the model has just output i as original token 2-4, so recall_idx is 3-5. It is strongest at recall_idx 3, where the top examples all have i at original position 2, and it gets weaker at later positions. It almost never fires on the final output step (to_go == 0). It never fires in the original phase or on <DEL>, never on the first occurrence of i, and essentially never for other tokens. Dev split: F1 0.87, mass recall 0.97.

issues: The claims check out on dev. All activation mass is in the copy phase (none in the original phase or on <DEL>). 99.8% of the mass has in_tok == i. in_first == 0 holds for every activation, though this is trivially true because a copy-phase i always appeared earlier in the original. Mass by recall_idx: 0.59 at 3, 0.36 at 4, 0.04 at 5, and 0.007 at 2.

Precision of (phase==2 & in_tok==i) by recall_idx and L, i.e. P(active), when to_go >= 1: recall_idx 3 gives 0.95-1.0 for L >= 5, and recall_idx 4 gives 0.92-1.0 for L >= 6. When to_go == 0 it collapses: recall_idx 3 at L=4 gives 0.39 and recall_idx 4 at L=5 gives 0.15. This confirms 'not on the last step'.

Mild overclaim: the label covers 'original token 2-4', but at recall_idx 5 (i at original position 4) the feature fires only 36-48% of the time, even with to_go >= 2. Those activations are weak (about 1.5% of mass), and splitting by digits seen, a vowel as prev_tok, or in_count >= 2 does not separate them. So they look like a graded falloff, not a separate pattern. The core of the feature is i at original positions 2-3. The explanation's 'weaker at later positions' partly covers this.

Test misses for the original predicate are scattered weak activations: low-activation i at other positions plus a few non-i tokens, 2.5% of mass in total. The false positives are mostly recall_idx 5 and some recall_idx 4 cases with to_go == 1. I found no systematic token, length or history class that is missed.

Alternative predicates add almost nothing. Restricting to recall_idx 3-4 with to_go >= 1 gives test precision 0.984, recall 0.776, F1 0.868. Adding recall_idx 5 only when to_go >= 2 gives test F1 0.873, against 0.867 for the original. The original predicate is essentially as good as it gets.
